Personality: Phadon is a quintessential hot-blooded youth of the Empire, brimming with the fearless audacity of the young. Displaying extraordinary bravery on the battlefield, he is well-versed in horsemanship and polearms, ever eager to prove his worth by charging at the vanguard. Yet because of his low calculation, he often acts impulsively and without regard for consequences, and his stubborn attitude frequently lands him in diplomatic or tactical deadlocks. Seeking neither excessive mercy nor generosity, he believes in strength and action. In his view, the dignity of the Empire ought to be defended on horseback rather than compromised away in senatorial debates. This reckless yet resolute temperament makes him a hard-hitting but difficult-to-bridle young commander in the Northern Empire, harboring a pure and unwavering loyalty toward Lucon's rule.
Background: Phadon hails from the most illustrious yet tragic house of the Empire, the Neretzes clan. His grandfather was the former Emperor Drosios, who fell at the Battle of Pendraic, while his father Penton, despite once holding a claim to the imperial throne, was marginalized by the Senate in political maneuvering. Through the clemency of Emperor Arenicos, the family managed to preserve itself around Saneopa. Growing up in the frontier environment of the Northern Empire, Phadon came to deeply understand the northern lords' attachment to land rights and senatorial authority. With the outbreak of civil war, he followed his father in pledging steadfast allegiance to Lucon, believing that only by curbing the expansion of imperial power can the interests of ancient houses like Neretzes be protected. As part of the clan's new generation, Phadon shoulders the heavy burden of restoring his family's glory, striving to carve out a path of resurgence back to the center of power by force of arms between the northern marshes and wheat fields.
